findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The three-door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Crab Rangoon filling probed to be at 50F. Raw beef probed to be at 51F. The TCS food items in the cooler will be discarded. An employee stated that they will be taking the tofu, eggs, and meat in the cooler home. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The three-door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Raw beef was probed to be at a temperature of 51F and crab Rangoon filling probed to be at 50F. The TCS food items in the cooler will be voluntarily discarded. A follow up is scheduled for 7/10/2026 to ensure that the cooler is repaired and is properly cold holding. A spot check will be conducted on 7/9/2026 regarding the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: THIRD REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). An employee stated that they are currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: All three employees were observed to not use a barrier when turning off the faucet of the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The employees were educated on using a barrier when turning off the faucet to prevent contamination to clean hands. Ensure that staff are educated on proper handwashing procedures to prevent contamination to clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- An employee was observed to handle raw chicken with their gloves, wipe their gloves off with a towel, and then touch tongs and other items with the same gloves. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that after handling raw chicken, the gloves need to be discarded and hands should be washed before donning gloves again. 

An employee was observed to use their gloves to make a sanitizer bucket with bleach and touch the triple sink faucet handles, then proceed to prepare food. CORRECTED- The employee was educated to discard their gloves, wash their hands, and don gloves again before preparing food. 

Ensure that employees are properly educated on when to wash their hands. A handout was given that is translated to Thai and it is highly recommended to post this in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: The ice scoop was observed to have the handle in direct contact with the ice in the ice machine. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and an employee to have the handle of the ice scoop stored above the ice. The scoop handle was moved to be stored above the ice. Ensure that food is protected from contamination from bare-hand contact by having the scoop handle stored above the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was observed to be two chairs in front of the only handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The owner moved the chairs away from the handwashing sink and was educated about making sure the handwashing sink is accessible to employees at all times. Ensure that the handwashing sink is always accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a package of raw bacon on the top shelf of the three-door cooler above containers of sauces. CORRECTED- The bacon was moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler and proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There is a container of noodles that is observed to be stored uncovered in the three-door cooler and there is a container of wontons that is observed to be uncovered in the chest freezer. When opening the chest freezer door, there is frost from the door that is falling onto the wontons. This was discussed with the PIC.  Ensure that food is stored in covered containers, wrappings, or packages to protect them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen tested to be at 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 150ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that the sanitizer is frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. It is recommended to remake the sanitizer buckets every two to four hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple cutting boards stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. CORRECTED- The cutting boards were moved from behind the faucet and will be washed, rinsed, and sanitized before being placed with the clean dishes. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was an opened bottle of Golden Mountain Seasoning Sauce, two opened bottles of Unagi Sushi Sauce, and an opened bottle of Hoison Sauce that were observed to be stored at room temperature and their labels stated to “Refrigerate After Opening”. CORRECTED- These bottles of sauces were discarded and the PIC was educated to read the label after opening the food item. Storing these sauces in the cooler in the future was discussed. Ensure that TCS foods are stored at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There are multiple boxes of food items that are observed to be stored on the floor throughout the kitchen. The kitchen is very cluttered and there is not enough storage for all of the items in the kitchen. Ensure that food items are stored at least six inches above the ground. It is recommended to reduce the clutter in the kitchen to allow for more storage space.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment:
The employee and owner were observed to make a sanitizer bucket using Purell sanitizer, but did not have any test strips for the sanitizer. It was discussed to cease using the Purell sanitizer unless test strips have been obtained for it. 

The facility is also observed to be using Quaternary ammonium sanitizer, but do not have any Quaternary ammonium test strips for the sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 7/8/2026 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are test strips available for every type of sanitizer that is utilized in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The gaskets of the doors of the larger preparation cooler in the kitchen. 
2. The standing white freezer needs to be defrosted. 
3. The bottom of the three-door cooler. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The hood baffles. These are observed to have an accumulation of grease on them. Ensure that these are cleaned before they begin to drip and contaminate cooking food. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The floor behind and under the cook-line equipment. This was shown to the PIC. There is significant accumulation of grease and food debris under and behind the cook-line. Ensure that this is cleaned to prevent pest harborage conditions. 
3. The floor in the mop sink area is observed to be in need of cleaning. 

Ensure that physical facilities are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There is observed to be personal items mixed in with items intended for the restaurant in the three-door cooler. Personal storage was discussed with the PIC and the majority of the items were moved to be on the bottom shelf. Ensure that personal items are stored in the bottom of the cooler away from items for the facility to prevent contamination to food.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC stated that the other PIC is currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to use their gloved hands to roll their sleeves of their shirt up and continued to prepare food using the soiled gloves. CORRECTED- Handwashing education was conducted with the PIC and the employee. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable of when to wash their hands and change gloves to avoid contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container holding packages of raw chicken above containers of mushrooms in the bottom of a preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The container of the packages of chicken was moved to be on the bottom shelf of another cooler. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order. Food should be protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was a clean cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. CORRECTED- The cutting board was moved from behind the faucet and the PIC stated that it would be washed, rinsed, and sanitized before being used. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were six containers of orange chicken sauce that were made in-house that had a date-marking of 3/11/2026 on them. CORRECTED- The containers of orange chicken sauce were discarded and the PIC was educated that food items made in the facility can only be held for up to 7 days before they must be discarded, with day 1 being the date of preparation or opening and the item being discarded at the end of the 7th day (think day 1 + 6 days). Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items are being date-marked and are being used or discarded by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There is not a probe thermometer available in the facility. It is important to have a probe thermometer to ensure that food is being cooked to the correct temperature. A follow up is scheduled for 4/10/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer is obtained. Education for calibration of the thermometer will be conducted as well.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The shelf liners that hold clean glasses were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. Discussed ceasing use of liners or obtaining liners that are smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces that are exposed to splash and spillage are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not a prepared sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen for sanitizing food-contact surfaces. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. The PICs were educated that there should always be a sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen, before food preparation or cooking even begins. It is essential to have a prepared sanitizer bucket that is at a label-recommended concentration to clean food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

1. The hood baffles. These are observed to have an accumulation of grease on them. Ensure that these are cleaned before they begin to drip and contaminate cooking food. 
2. The floor behind and under the cook-line equipment. This was shown to the PIC. There is significant accumulation of grease and food debris under and behind the cook-line. Ensure that this is cleaned to prevent pest harborage conditions.

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: One of the PICs was observed to prepare spring rolls using their bare hands and the PIC stated that the spring rolls will not be cooked before being served. CORRECTED- The spring rolls that were prepared were discarded and the PIC was educated that ready-to-eat foods should not be handled with bare hands. Bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods can lead to foodborne illness. Ready-to-eat foods should be handled with utensils or gloved hands (with the hands being washed prior to gloves being donned.)
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was a lemon in the handwashing sink and the ice machine was observed to be draining into this handwashing sink as well. The lemon was removed and this was discussed with the PIC. Handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. A follow up is scheduled for 12/5/2025 to ensure that the ice machine is draining into another sink or bucket.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility has par-cooked chicken in a foil pan that was observed to not be in cold or hot holding. The PIC stated that they make more of the chicken as they run out and they cook it before serving. The PIC stated that they do not always go through it within the four hours that is allotted under Time as Control. This was discussed with the PIC, as this should either be hot held, cold held, or placed under Time as Control. CORRECTED- The chicken had only been there since 12pm, when the facility opened, and was placed under Time as Control. The operator stated that they will begin putting it in the cooler and cold holding it. A spot check will be conducted on 12/5/2025 to ensure that the chicken is being cold held after it is cooked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were containers of sauces that were cooked and then cooled that did not have date-marking on them. CORRECTED- The items were date-marked during the inspection. All Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods that are opened or prepared in an establishment should be date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening and day 7 being the date the item is discarded. A spot check will be conducted on 12/5/2025 to ensure that TCS items that are held for over 24 hours are being date-marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: The facility uses a container of water to hold their rice-scoop in between uses. The PIC stated that they change the rice-scoop water a few times throughout the day, but there was no written indication or standard operating procedure of when this rice-scoop water is changed. Ensure that there is a written indication of when items that are under Time as Control were made to make sure they are being discarded of after 4 hours. A follow up is scheduled for 12/5/2025 to ensure that the time is being recorded for the rice-scoop water.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There are dishes and single-service containers throughout the kitchen that have their food-contact surfaces exposed to contamination. This was discussed with the PICs. Ensure that these items are inverted to protect the food-contact surfaces from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

The PICs were educated that there should always be a sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen, before food preparation or cooking even begins. It is essential to have a prepared sanitizer bucket that is at a label-recommended concentration to clean food-contact surfaces.

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Employee reporting agreements were observed to not be signed. CORRECTED- All present employees signed one and there are only a few other employees. The PIC stated that they will have the other employees sign when they come to work. Ensure that these are kept in a safe space, as they will need to be accessed for all future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC stated that the other PIC is currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The PIC did not have signed employee reporting agreements for any of the three employees currently working at the facility. This was discussed with the operator and copies were provided. A follow up will be conducted on 9/2/2025 to ensure that there is a signed employee reporting agreement for all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of raw chicken skewers above containers of peanut sauce. CORRECTED- These were moved to the bottom shelf next to the other raw chicken in the cooler and education was conducted regarding storage order. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There were clean cutting boards stored behind the faucets of the triple sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- These cutting boards were cleaned and moved onto a dish shelf to be stored. This was discussed with the PIC and they were educated that the wall and faucet the cutting boards were touching are not clean surfaces. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility holds their bean sprouts on an ice bath due to lack of cooler space. The bean sprouts are in water in a container, which is sitting on ice. The ice bath did not sufficiently submerge the bottom of the container of the bean sprouts to allow for proper cold holding. The bean sprouts were probed to be at 60F at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated on how to properly make an ice bath to allow for proper cold holding. The ice bath needs to submerge the sides of the container. The ice bath was corrected and the sprouts were probed to be at 41F. Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There is not a probe thermometer available in the facility. It is important to have a probe thermometer to ensure that food is being cooked to the correct temperature. A follow up is scheduled for 9/2/2025 to ensure that a probe thermometer is obtained. Education for calibration of the thermometer will be conducted as well.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility does not have test strips for the sanitizer that they are using. They are currently using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer and need to have Quaternary ammonium test strips available to check the concentration of the sanitizer. If using another type of sanitizer (such as Lactic Acid or bleach (Chlorine)), you also need test strips for that type of sanitizer. The PIC was educated on this and was shown photos of what the test strips look like. A follow up is scheduled for 9/2/2025 to ensure that test strips have been obtained for the sanitizers used within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: REPEAT- The stainless steel wall covering to the wall left of the wok is observed to be in need of being sealed to the wall. Ensure that this is sealed and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
